CORRECTION TO THE NOTE ABOVE: one word was blanked. The line should read "StorySourceView.scala:65-66
filters ALL to supported nodes before anything derives from it". I wrote the identifier in backticks
inside a double-quoted shell string and the shell executed it -- the THIRD time today. Twice I noted
it and carried on; noting it has evidently not worked, so from here every mote body and commit
message goes through a heredoc file, which is a mechanism rather than an intention.

The bead's substance stands as written. Restating the part that matters, intact:

WHAT REMAINS, unassigned and available: signature.scala:392 and population.scala:271 both declare

    val discoursePos: SourceNodeRef => Option[Double] = r => Some(view.relativePosition(r))

an Option that structurally cannot be None, one line above a worldPos that uses the same absence
channel correctly. The SourceView totality law landed at a9f20a5 now guarantees relativePosition is
meaningful for every exposed ref, so the honest fix is probably to DROP the Option rather than thread
None through it. Check worldPos first -- it genuinely needs its Option.

OCCURS IS MEASURED AND NEGATIVE. StorySourceView.scala:65-66 filters the node vector to supported
nodes before anything else derives from it, so node(ref) is total over every ref the view exposes and
the branch cannot fire today. Permits yes, occurs no, consumes yes. A type-honesty fix, not a live
bug, and the commit should say so rather than implying a defect was firing.
